title: Few organs lack any known transitional grade

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Few organs lack any known transitional grade

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Despite the small proportion of living and known forms relative to extinct and unknown ones, it is rare to find an organ toward which no transitional grade is known to lead.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I have been astonished how rarely an organ can be named, towards which no transitional grade is known to lead.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Natura non facit saltum.”. Scope: organs of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A sample-based estimate is possible, but global coverage across plant and animal organs is poor. Coding transitional grades requires substantial interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a representative inventory of organ systems and score whether extant or fossil taxa exhibit ordered structural grades approaching each system. Estimate the fraction lacking any known grade, with preregistered rules for what counts as transitional.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The terms 'rarely' and 'towards' allow subjective coding.

No complete standardized inventory of organs and grades exists.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.48
data existence: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Matrices exist for well-studied character systems, so a subset of organs can be scored, but the claim is a frequency across organs in general. Building that sampling frame would take years of literature coding, and failure to find a grade does not mean none exists. Discriminating power stays low because the result tracks the history of description as much as biology.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Draw a sample of named organs across plants and animals and score whether a structurally intermediate form is known in a relative. The claim is supported if that fraction is high; it is weakened if a large share of organs, after a defined search, still lacks any intermediate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Absence of a known grade is confounded by research effort and preservation.

What counts as an organ or a transitional grade is not standardized.

No dataset enumerates organs across plants and animals.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.32
data adequacy: 0.32
data existence: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.42
